reviewer_model: galaxy-light subtraction (photutils isophotes, no AI model)
what_i_see: After subtracting an elliptical-isophote model of the compact red host, a curved arc remains just south of it in VIS (peak 19 sigma), with a compact counterpart in Y (9 sigma) and H (11 sigma) at the arc's brightest knot.
most_likely: A real curved feature about 1 arcsec from the host, relatively brighter in VIS than in NISP, so bluer than the host, as expected for a lensed background star-forming galaxy.
against_it: The isophote fit absorbed part of the arc and over-subtracted the north side, so a counter-image cannot be assessed; a masked or parametric fit is needed. A tidal feature or a projected companion is also possible.
decisive_test: Parametric lens and host modelling of the full-depth VIS frame with the arc masked, looking for a counter-image north of the host; a spectrum of the arc.
catalogue_notes: No SIMBAD or NED entry within 10 arcsec; nearest ECLIPSE lens 484 arcsec away. Image rows of panels: VIS, Y, H residuals, 8 x 8 arcsec, north up.
